question_options.question: How would you rate this pack?
Are you graduating from high school this year?

nodes.text: Spike leaves the library.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I hope I'm ready!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Yeah, I can be your 'in' to all the hot summer parties! You can hang out with the cool kids.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Imagine this. Loud, jammin' music, drinks with cute umbrellas, a thirst-quenching pool...

nodes.speaker: Erik
nodes.text: You can drink pool water?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: It's just a phrase.

nodes.speaker: Erik
nodes.text: I don't think...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: But besides the pool, you'll be surrounded by a ton of cute girls!

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: Uh, that's okay, Spike. My ears are sensitive to loud music , Erik's afraid of deep water, and Brendan's not interested in other girls.

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: Besides, can you imagine us dancing to music? Or intentionally soaking up sun rays?

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: I mean, parties where you talk to people are fun, but not as much fun as blasting aliens together...

nodes.speaker: Erik
nodes.text: Or pinning the tail on the donkey!

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: But thanks for the offer, Spike. Good luck studying!
Spike walks to a far table in the back of the library and opens his books.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Well, it's all up to me now...
Spike cracks open a book entitled 'Death of a Spring Queen'...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: 'In the before time, when the skies cracked open their blue eyes for the first time...'

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: 'And when the earth flourished, untouched by naught but the hand of the godkind...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Yaaaaawn. Oh, boy, this is going to be tough...
Later, Spike picks up another novel entitled 'The Glass Slipper' and opens it.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: 'Life is not to be held but experienced. Like cupping your hands around water...'

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: 'The droplets leak through until all you have left is the memory of that which you have touched...'

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Got to stay awake!
Later, Spike picks up another paper on English terms and studies it.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: 'Alliteration' is when words have the same first letter or syllable. 'Dystopia' is...
Until at last, it's evening.

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: Video equipment?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I know how you nerds like electronics. You can totally borrow her stuff.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Mallika has a nice camera, some spot lights, a computer program to help you edit the film...

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: We did come up with this great idea for a screenplay...

nodes.speaker: Erik
nodes.text: We're calling it `Space 'Splosions: The Sequel Movie 2!`
nodes.text_bbcode: We're calling it [color=#e23b3b][i]Space 'Splosions: The Sequel Movie 2![/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Erik
nodes.text: It opens up on the stalwart Captain Quarch, as he's steering the Undertaking and taking it to parts unknown...

nodes.speaker: Erik
nodes.text: When he stumbles across an alien planet in need of his assistance!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: That, er, sounds great...

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: With Mallika's equipment, we could make it really good.

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: We could even make it so the astro-guns shoot real lasers!

nodes.speaker: Erik
nodes.text: I already made most of the costumes... It only took one roll of aluminum foil!

nodes.speaker: Erik
nodes.text: But who's going to be the alien?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Tell you what, if you give me some pointers for the final, I'll even act in your video.

nodes.speaker: Erik
nodes.text: Whee! The green hair would be perfect!

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: So we have a deal. Let's start with the first novel, 'Death of a Spring Queen' in which Queen Persephone eats the poisoned pomegranate...
And for the next couple hours, Spike and the nerds cover all the material on the English final.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: So you're saying the theme of the novel 'The Glass Slipper' is about transience and the fragility of life...

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: Yes!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: So the book is about the destruction of the world through human folly?

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: Yes. It shows a dystopia, or a vision of the world at its very worst...
Until at last...

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: Think you got all that?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Yeah! Thanks guys! You can come pick up the camera equipment this weekend after graduation!

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: Pleasure doing business with you.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Isn't that where they're supposed to study?

nodes.speaker: Justin
nodes.text: Well, yes, but running a short-order business is distracting and noisy, and they're interfering with others who want to study.

nodes.speaker: Justin
nodes.text: If only there were some way to limit their usage... Oh! We charge `them` a small fee to use the library!
nodes.text_bbcode: If only there were some way to limit their usage... Oh! We charge [color=#e23b3b][i]them[/i][/color] a small fee to use the library!

nodes.speaker: Justin
nodes.text: I'm so brilliant some days I scare myself.

nodes.speaker: Scott
nodes.text: We're definitely going to have to talk about that.

nodes.speaker: Scott
nodes.text: Anyway, thanks for the input, Spike. It's good to keep local dictators in check.

nodes.speaker: Scott
nodes.text: Good luck studying for finals!
$Scott and Justin walk off, arguing.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I guess I should start studying for that final on Friday...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Hey, if the nerds are offering tutoring sessions... Maybe they can help me!
Spike grabs his English books from his locker and heads to the library.
Inside, the nerds have set up three tables, each labeled with posters of different school subjects.
Spike heads to the one labeled 'English' and finds Dex wrapping up a session as Erik counts money.

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: And the last term is 'hyperbole'. That just means you exaggerate something.

nodes.speaker: Zach
nodes.text: Ugh, this is ridiculous! It's going to take me a million years to learn all these words!

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: There you go! `That` was a hyperbole!
nodes.text_bbcode: There you go! [color=#e23b3b][i]That[/i][/color] was a hyperbole!

nodes.speaker: Zach
nodes.text: ...I have never been this confused in my life.
Zach leaves dejectedly.

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: Can't win 'em all.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Uh, Dex, Erik? I have a test on Friday. Can you help me out?

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: We help everyone out... For a fee! So what is it? A science lab test? A history final?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: An English exam. For fourth year English.

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: Yes! That's an easy final. As long as you've read the books, you'll be fine.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: ...And if you haven't read the books?

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: Well, you won't be so fine. But that's what tutoring's for. So if you just pay a certain amount, we can get started.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Uh... I'm a little strapped for cash right now. Is there anything else I can give you?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I could teach you all to skate!

nodes.speaker: Erik
nodes.text: I'd prefer to stay on the ground please.

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: Sorry, Spike. I tried skating once.

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: I don't think my dad will ever forgive me for taking out his favorite hunting dog.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Yikes. So that's a definite 'no', huh?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Hmmm.... Come on, there's gotta be something I can give them. These guys are nerds. What would they want?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Well, I'm a pretty connected guy. I can hook you guys up with...

nodes.prompt: I can hook you up with...

menu.title: Make your choice!
menu.text: I can hook you up with...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Justin might be right on this one.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Extortion doesn't sound like a good word.

nodes.speaker: Justin
nodes.text: I'm glad the buffoon agrees with me.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Hey!

nodes.speaker: Scott
nodes.text: Maybe it isn't, but...

nodes.speaker: Scott
nodes.text: They're not violating a school rule. It's not like we have a say in it.

nodes.speaker: Justin
nodes.text: But don't we have any say in how they're using the library?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: $Scott sounds like he does have a point.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: If the nerds are the ones tutoring, then maybe they deserve to get paid.

nodes.speaker: Justin
nodes.text: I'm not saying they don't deserve it. But do they really have to do it in the library?

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: I have to say, Spike, I'm really disappointed in you.

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: You've had an entire year to fulfill the requirements you missed, and you still can't graduate?

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: What are you going to do now?

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: How are you going to fix this?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Mom, I'll think of something. If it's a mistake, I'll correct it. And if it's not... I'll figure it out.

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: I hope you do. At this rate, `Chip` is going to catch up to you.
nodes.text_bbcode: I hope you do. At this rate, [color=#3b78e2][i]Chip[/i][/color] is going to catch up to you.

nodes.speaker: Chip
nodes.text: Heck yeah, I am!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#e23b3b][i]!!![/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: And I hate to say this, but if you don't graduate this year, I don't think I'll be able to keep supporting you.

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: Even though I still have my job, it's not enough. I need your help, and I need to know I can count on you.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Oh, I'm sorry, mom.

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: First thing tomorrow, you're going to see Ms. Lee.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Yes, mom.
She drops the letter off with Spike, then heads into the kitchen.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Sorry you had to hear that, Mallika.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: You okay?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Not really. You heard my mom. What if I don't graduate? What am I going to do?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Oh, Spike... What have you been doing all school year? I thought you were getting everything done.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I thought I was too.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Maybe we can sort this all out. Can I take a look?
Mallika reads over the letter.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Wait a minute, Spike. I think you can still graduate.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: The letter just says you have to do these last three requirements before the end of the week.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Requirements? What requirements?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: All you have to do is make up your P.E. hours, do your community service, and pass English.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: But I haven't been to P.E. in a while, I don't do community service, and...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I didn't pass English?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: It says you're borderline. You just have to pass the final exam on Friday.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Which I didn't study for.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: But it's not hopeless, Spike.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: As long as you meet these requirements you'll graduate! You should ask Ms. Lee what you can do!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: All right!
After school the next day, in Ms. Lee's office...

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Unless you fulfill these requirements, Spike, we can't give you a high school diploma.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: And without one of those... Well, you'll end up making poor choices, eventually trying for your GED, cobbling together some sort of degree...

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: And living out your days counseling children to make better decisions than you did.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Er...

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: So that's it. It's not an error, Spike. You won't graduate this year.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Wait, Ms. Lee, isn't there something I can do to change that?

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Well, let's take a look. You're about to fail English unless you can pass your final exam on Friday...

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Which I'm assuming you haven't studied for.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Then you need to get your P.E. credits in line, which is near impossible in the three days you have left.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: And finally, as a senior, you were supposed to fulfill your community service hours.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Okay, Ms. Lee, you're right about the first two, but I've definitely been doing community service all year.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Not nearly enough, and the office still has no report from a supervisor proving you have been working.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Ms. Lee, come on. I don't want to stay here `another` year.
nodes.text_bbcode: Ms. Lee, come on. I don't want to stay here [color=#e23b3b][i]another[/i][/color] year.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: I'm sorry, but unless you really work hard for the next three days getting everything done, I'm afraid that's it.
Spike stands up.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I'm motivated, Ms. Lee. I'll find a way to finish all these requirements on time.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: I hope you do.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Bye bye now!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Looks like I have my work cut out for me!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: But what do I do first?
Spike walks down the hall and runs into $Scott and Justin!

nodes.speaker: Scott
nodes.text: I don't know, Justin. I'd relax about the whole thing. Let the nerds have their fun.

nodes.speaker: Justin
nodes.text: It's our responsibility to make sure that...

nodes.speaker: Scott
nodes.text: We don't let people have too much fun?

nodes.speaker: Justin
nodes.text: I didn't say that.

nodes.speaker: Justin
nodes.text: We've been arguing this point all morning, $Scott. Nothing's going to get settled at this rate.
$Scott turns to Spike.

nodes.speaker: Scott
nodes.text: Hey, Spike, want to settle something for us?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Sure.

nodes.speaker: Justin
nodes.text: The nerds have been using the library to run their black market tutoring league, charging students exorbitant amounts for information.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Ha ha, awesome!

nodes.speaker: Justin
nodes.text: `Not` awesome. Don't you think it's improper for the nerds to extort their fellow students?
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#e23b3b][i]Not[/i][/color] awesome. Don't you think it's improper for the nerds to extort their fellow students?

nodes.speaker: Scott
nodes.text: Or do you think the nerds should be able to charge for their tutoring services?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Uh... The nerds...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I signed up for all the classes I was supposed to! I made sure of it!

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: Then why aren't you on track to graduate?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I don't know! But I'll take care of this.

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: Good!

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: It's about time you take responsibility for your actions.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Ms. Lee probably made a mix up. She has a few screws loose, if you know what I mean.

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: Are you calling your guidance counselor crazy?

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: Don't you find that a little immature at your age?

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: And even if she is mixed-up, there's no mistake that your name is at the top of this form.

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: So at the very least, I expect you to talk to her about it.
It's the last few days before graduation, and everyone is busy!
Since finals are around the corner, the nerds are getting a ton of requests for tutoring sessions.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: It seems like all my classmates want my help studying for the science final. I don't have enough time to tutor everyone!

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: No, but... I just thought of a way we can make this profitable for us...

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: What are you thinking?

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: The plan goes like this...
And meanwhile, in the cafeteria, the sports teams are setting up for the year-end athletic banquet...

nodes.speaker: Kim
nodes.text: All right, we need to set up fifty tables, and we don't have all day to do it!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Get moving, swim team!
And the graduating seniors are getting their robes and mortarboards in preparation for the big day...

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: No more homework, no more tests...

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: No more books!

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: Not if you're starting community college in the fall, doofus.

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: I heard you can skip classes whenever you want!

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: If you're happy about that, you're dumber than I thought. We skip classes now...
And at the Chapman house, Spike and Mallika talk about graduation and their summer plans.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Just think... One more week of classes and finals, and we'll be done with high school forever.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Wow, that's a thought.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: So what are your big plans after we graduate?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Well, right after the ceremony, my mom wants to throw me a party at our house...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I meant, after that. You know, next year.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Oh, I'm not sure yet. I need to pick a college, but I'm waiting for Oxfjord to get back to me.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Oxfjord? Is that a school in Europe?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: It's only the greatest university in Norway! It sits on top of some of the most beautiful natural fjords in the world!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Isn't that a little dangerous?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: And exciting!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: It'll be so fun to travel abroad and learn a new language! And I'll be miles away from home and...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Me.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: That does make me sad, Spike. But we have all summer to hang out, and we'll spend time together on breaks. Are you going to be okay here in Centerscore?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I'll just be happy if I graduate, honestly. After what happened last time...

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Don't worry, Spike. You have everything in order this year, right?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Uh...
At that moment, Mrs. Chapman and Chip bursts into the room, startling both teens.

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: Spike Chapman! You have some explaining to do!

nodes.speaker: Chip
nodes.text: You are in `so` much trouble, bro.
nodes.text_bbcode: You are in [color=#e23b3b][i]so[/i][/color] much trouble, bro.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: What?

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: I just received a letter from Ms. Lee, and she says that you're not going to graduate because you failed to complete the required coursework.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Aw man, not again! I did everything they told me... Well, mostly.

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: How could you do this? I accepted that you had to stay back one year, but `two?!`
nodes.text_bbcode: How could you do this? I accepted that you had to stay back one year, but [color=#3b78e2][i]two?![/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Mom...
And for the next two hours, Spike successfully supports the basketball team!
In the first quarter...
Spike passes the ball to Jacob who goes in for a layup!

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: Solid pass, Spike.
Later...
Spike guards a man on the other team... Leaving Kenji free to steal the ball!

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: Nice pick!
After halftime...
Spike grabs the rebound of a missed shot and makes a sharp pass to Andy!
Andy sinks it, and Centerscore wins!

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: Yeah!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I am a beast on this court!
At the end of the game, over on the sidelines...

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: You did pretty good out there for a beginner.

nodes.speaker: Phil
nodes.text: I'll say. You didn't get in our way at all. That's more than good.

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: Yeah, great work, Spike. You were really solid out there.

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: You sure you want to graduate? We can use you next year.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Ha ha. I have to move on. It's too bad though. This was a lot of fun.

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: Well, nothing we can do about it now. Come on, let's go celebrate!
The boys head out, laughing and cheering over their win.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: We can't stop the future from happening. We can only move on with our lives.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I guess you're right.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Whatever happens, Mallika, I'm glad I'm with you now.
Spike and Mallika kiss.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Why? What do you think will happen?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Well, you're going to Norway to attend Oxfjord...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: And I'm staying here.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: We can still date, of course.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I don't know, Mallika. Everyone tells me that long-distance things don't work.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Oh.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Great, that just made Mallika and me `both` sad!
nodes.text_bbcode: Great, that just made Mallika and me [color=#e23b3b][i]both[/i][/color] sad!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I don't know what I'm going to do after I graduate, Mallika.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: It's all been one big adventure in high school. I always knew what my goals were and what I wanted.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: But it's all different now that I'm graduating.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Spike, we all feel that way. I understand what you're going through.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: But you have a plan...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I haven't even thought about what I'm going to do now.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: It doesn't mean I'm not nervous about the future...

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: But, Spike, it's not as bad as all that. Don't worry.
Spike goes on to fill out the rest of the test.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Prez
nodes.text: All right, girls and boys. Turn your papers in.
Spike turns his paper in with the rest as the bell rings for the next class.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: That was not as hard as I thought...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I think I passed!
At the end of the day, Spike finds his English teacher, Ms. Prez.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Hey, Ms. Prez? I really need a good grade to graduate...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: So, did I get a 'C'?

nodes.speaker: Ms. Prez
nodes.text: Well, you didn't get a 'C'...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: What? But I studied and...

nodes.speaker: Ms. Prez
nodes.text: You got a B+! Great work, Spike. I'm glad you really picked up your performance for the final.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Prez
nodes.text: See you later.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Yeah!
Spike walks out.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: How could I have forgotten what I just studied?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Hopefully I got a 'C' on that...
Spike walks out.
In the parking lot, Spike meets up with Mallika.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Spike! There you are! I've been texting you all afternoon!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: You look excited. What happened?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: I just found out... I got into Oxfjord! They accepted me! I get my own room and everything, and...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Congrats! That's great! You've always wanted to go there.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Yeah, I'll be moving away in August. It'll be really fun to get away and live in a foreign country.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: I'm just really excited.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: So... How'd your final go?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Great! Smooth. Like grinding down a rail.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: And you know what's even better?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: That was your last final! Ever!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: You're right. It was! The last test...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I could've done better, but maybe I'll still pass.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Have confidence, Spike.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: But you know what will make you feel better?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: That was your last final! Ever!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Well, if I passed it.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: I'm sure you did fine.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Then it's definitely the last test...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: The last class... The last thing I ever have to do at Centerscore!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: The last thing I ever get to do here.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: You sound down.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Well, this is one of the last times we'll ever be here, Mallika.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: It just makes me a little sad and worried.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: What are you worried about?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Was it that answer or something else?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Yeah, that's what Dex was saying. A vision of the world where dark things happen.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I nailed this question!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Was it that answer or something else?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: The next question is...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: 'A dystopia is...'

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Was that it? I could've sworn it was about something else...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Was that it? I could've sworn it was about something else...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: 'Fragility' like how something made of glass is fragile!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Yes!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Next question.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: The theme of 'The Glass Slipper' is...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Yes! Queen Persephone had to die from something...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: It must be the 'poisoned' one.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: That doesn't seem right.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Oh well, maybe I'll come back to it later...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: That doesn't seem right.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Oh well, maybe I'll come back to it later...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Yeah, by myself... I just hope it was enough.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: I received a report from your superior.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: True to expectations, she didn't seem that enthusiastic about your performance.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: She even said you didn't manage to complete your entire job, though you were given more than enough time.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: But since we don't require that you have to do your community service well, I'm still going to run this report past the principal.
And stops short!
In front of Spike lies the park's lake. A narrow bridge spans the lake on one side.
Spike runs toward the bridge, but backs up when he sees Travis!

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: Nowhere to run now!
Spike turns around and finds Ryan!

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: Get ready to eat pond scum!
Spike looks around frantically and looks to the lake for answers.
He spies shallow rocks in the water that cut across the lake to safe, dry land.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Those look slippery, but if I can run forward on the rocks, I can skirt past these bullies!
Spike does the only thing he can! He turns and deftly darts across the rocks!

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: He's walking on water!

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: No, you idiot. He's walking on rocks! Follow him!
Spike nimbly jumps from rock to rock, until his feet touch dry land!
Behind him, struggling to stay balanced, Travis teeters on the slippery rocks and reaches out to grab Ryan's arm!

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: No, lugnuts!
Travis and Ryan go down with a splash! Ryan comes up sputtering for air.

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: You idiot! What'd you drag me down for?!

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: You could've held me up.

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: You're a gorilla! You'd have torn me in half if I tried to hold you up!

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: You didn't have to call me a 'gorilla'.
Spike takes this opportunity to escape.
Back at the skate park, Spike cleans the graffiti with renewed vigor.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Without those goons on my back, this job's pretty easy!
A couple hours later, the wall is clean.

nodes.speaker: Denni
nodes.text: Hey, I just came to check up on you...

nodes.speaker: Denni
nodes.text: Wow, this is great! It looks like new!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Hey, I just put a little elbow grease into it.

nodes.speaker: Denni
nodes.text: I'll say. Hey, if you don't have too many plans, you should join W.H.A.L.E. for the summer!

nodes.speaker: Denni
nodes.text: We could use someone with your dedication.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I'll definitely think about it!

nodes.speaker: Denni
nodes.text: Anyway, great job. I'll let Ms. Lee know!
Denni walks away.
Spike does the only thing he can! He turns and sprints across the rocks!
But the rocks are too slippery for good footing, and he goes down with a large splash!

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: That was the best show ever!

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: Ha ha ha!
When Spike comes up sputtering for air, Ryan and Travis each grab one of his arms.

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: You're coming with us!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Hey, wait, where are you taking me?!

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: To the other side of town!
Ryan and Travis shove Spike into the back of their car.
A couple hours later...
Spike trudges back to the park, bedraggled and slightly damp.
He finds Denni waiting with the sponges and soap.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Denni, you wouldn't believe the time I just had...

nodes.speaker: Denni
nodes.text: I'll tell you what I can't believe, Spike. How could you just ditch your job like that?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Whoa, hang on, wait a minute... I'd have finished except that Ryan and Travis took me across town.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: And then I had to fight all these strange characters... It was weird.

nodes.speaker: Denni
nodes.text: Ryan and Travis brought you all the way across town to meet weird people?!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Uh, no!

nodes.speaker: Denni
nodes.text: You know, if you didn't want to volunteer, then you didn't have to.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I'm not making this up! But I know the job's not done. Just give me a couple hours, and...

nodes.speaker: Denni
nodes.text: It's too late. I already have another team here to do the clean-up that you didn't do.
Denni walks away.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Well, looks like it's time to go home!
Back in Ms. Lee's office...

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Spike, I was just about to call you down here.
Spike dodges the baby stroller and keeps running, without breaking pace!
Behind him, Spike can hear the wail of a baby as Ryan and Travis thunder past!
Spike picks up his pace, sprinting around a bend...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Gahhh!
Spike screeches to a hard stop to let the mother and her stroller pass by.
A moment later, he picks up his speed, but Ryan and Travis close in!

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: Stopping for a baby? Lame!

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: We're going to grab you now, loser!
Spike sprints round a bend...
He spares a glance back to see Ryan and Travis sprinting after him.
When Spike looks forward again, he sees a baby stroller and a distracted mother crossing his path!
Spike waffles between the two, but darts left towards the children's playground.
He weaves in between parents and children, trying to stay ahead.

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: I can see him!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I bet I could've lost them if I'd gone through the trees...
Ryan and Travis gain speed and nearly take over Spike!

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: Nearly got you now!
Spike jumps away from Ryan, only to step onto a sand castle that a handful of children are building.
Behind him, children start crying.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Sorry, kids!
Spike keeps running.
Spike runs right into the trees, plunging into the underbrush and fighting back branches.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Urggg....
Behind him, Spike can hear Ryan and Travis having trouble navigating the thick leaves.

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: Where is he?! I can barely see!

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: I hate nature!

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: Less talking, more branch whacking!
Spike stumbles out the other side of the grove and keeps running.
Spike runs deeper into the park!
Half a minute later...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Huff... Huff...
Spike spares a glance back.

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: Come on, he's slowing down! We're gaining on him!
Spike flees further into the park, but stops short when he comes to a fork in the path!
To the left is a children's playground. To the right is a grove of trees.
Spike ducks under the punch and weaves hard to the left.

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: Don't let the punk get away!

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: I won't!
Abandoning the cleaning supplies, Spike runs off with Travis and Ryan on his tail!
Spike tries to jump away, but Travis' fist lands in his gut!
Spike is thrown back a couple feet from the impact!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: `Ahhh!`
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#e23b3b][i]Ahhh![/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: Again! Sock him one!
Staggering, Spike runs off as best he can, Travis and Ryan on his tail!
Travis lunges at Spike and tries to punch him!

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: Like what?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: You could toilet paper a house...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Toothpaste a car door...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Plastic wrap an old lady?

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: Hey, that stuff sounds like kinda cool...

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: 'Kinda cool'? `That` is kid stuff, my friend.
nodes.text_bbcode: 'Kinda cool'? [color=#e23b3b][i]That[/i][/color] is kid stuff, my friend.

nodes.text: Ryan waves his hand over their graffiti.

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: `This` is what we are capable of, Travis.
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#e23b3b][i]This[/i][/color] is what we are capable of, Travis.

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: None of that nonsense.

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: So toilet paper is a little eighth grade, but plastic wrap?

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: Don't you see what's happening here?

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: He's trying to get us to `not` graffiti.
nodes.text_bbcode: He's trying to get us to [color=#e23b3b][i]not[/i][/color] graffiti.

nodes.text: Travis turns to Spike.

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: I'm going to plastic wrap you!

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: What police?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: You know. Officer Monte? He's on patrol in this park right now.

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: He is?

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: I hate that guy!

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: But, Ryan, maybe we shouldn't stay here. If Monte busts us again...

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: I know, I know. We'll be in Boot Camp all summer.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: And wouldn't that suck.

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: Yeah... It would...
Travis turns away...
But Ryan pulls him back!

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: It would suck, but we're not gonna get caught. We just saw Monte.

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: He's on the other side of the park, remember?

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: Which means this twerp is lying.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Uh... There's a chance he might've followed you...

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: And there's a chance we might've spared your face...

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: But not anymore...

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: I came to watch your basketball game to see if your Coach would sign off on the papers.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: He said he'd never seen you before in his life, and he can't believe you'd jeopardize their morale by helping them lose.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: He accused you of being a pampered Wilson High kid if he'd ever seen one!

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: I'm sorry, Spike, but you'll just have to go to summer school to fulfill the P.E. requirement.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Yeah...
And for the next two hours...
Spike gets in the way of the basketball team!
Spike takes a wild shot! The ball bounces off the backboard and into the other team's hands!

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: Pass it next time, Spike. Kenji was wide and clear on your right.
Spike jumps in front of an opponent taking a shot and elbows him!
The opponent goes down.

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: What are you doing?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Stopping him from taking a shot?

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: Spike, that's a foul! It's like you're handing the other team points.
Spike tries to guard a guy but stands too far away!
The player breaks away from Spike, sets up his shot, and scores as the clock runs down.
The horn sounds, signaling the end of the game, and Spartan wins!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: This was our last game! Why did we recruit him again?

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: At this rate, a dummy could've done a better job.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Hey, I was just a stand-in. I didn't say I was any good. You took me on anyway.

nodes.speaker: Phil
nodes.text: He's right. He did stand in for us. Even if he did suck.

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: And thanks, but this is probably going to be a one-time thing.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Well, at least it's graduation. I'll be out of your way this time next week.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: `If` I graduate...
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#e23b3b][i]If[/i][/color] I graduate...

nodes.text: The next day, Spike enters Ms. Lee's office.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Good morning, Ms. Lee.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Spike! I have some news for you.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Well, that's the thing. Being part of the basketball team is going to help me graduate...

nodes.speaker: Phil
nodes.text: You need the P.E. credits?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Yeah.

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: No problem, man. You do well on the court tonight, and you'll be part of the team. I'll let Coach know.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Thanks!
That night, right before the start of the big basketball game...

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: All right, huddle up, you guys.

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: This is our last game before the season. Ever since we've picked up the pace with all that group-bonding stuff, this basketball team's done great!

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: So go out there and win!
Spike approaches Jacob.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Hey, Jacob, what am I doing?

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: You're going to be taking Erik's position.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Great. What position is that?

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: Well, Erik was technically our small forward... Sort of. He usually just ran around, claiming he was open.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Oh.

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: But, hey, that just means you don't really have to do much. Just help us out whenever you can.

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: You know, guard the opposite team, grab rebound balls, pick your shots, make the right passes...

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: And don't screw up.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Got it.
The boys run onto the court...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Here goes nothing...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: At least, I like watching it.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I'm more of a 'basketball watcher' than a 'basketball player'.

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: Well, it would be nice to have a player with some experience.

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: But I guess if you watch basketball, you know already some of the moves and strategies.

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: Besides, it's not like Erik knew the first thing about playing either.

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: Yeah, that guy was `awful.`
nodes.text_bbcode: Yeah, that guy was [color=#e23b3b][i]awful.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: But why did you choose now to join? Isn't the week right before graduation cutting it a little close?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I'm an adventurous guy. Sounded like fun.

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: So it just seemed like basketball `might` be your thing?
nodes.text_bbcode: So it just seemed like basketball [color=#e23b3b][i]might[/i][/color] be your thing?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: You know, I wouldn't put it like that.

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: You just felt like not trying out or joining practices or seeing what it was all about, and just planned on walking onto the team?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Don't get me wrong. I have a lot of respect for basketball.

nodes.speaker: Phil
nodes.text: Hey, Jacob, not everyone's a basketball star.

nodes.speaker: Phil
nodes.text: Besides we were just saying we needed a fifth guy anyway. And it's not like Erik was `that` good.
nodes.text_bbcode: Besides we were just saying we needed a fifth guy anyway. And it's not like Erik was [color=#e23b3b][i]that[/i][/color] good.

nodes.speaker: Phil
nodes.text: Enthusiastic, yes. Talented? Not really.

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: You're right, Phil. I shouldn't complain. We do need a fifth man.

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: But don't you think joining the team before graduation is a little late?
The next day in Ms. Lee's office...

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: Hey, Ms. Lee, I studied for my final. I have a good feeling about it, and I really think I can pass.

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: Excellent. It's that blind, senseless optimism that I admire about young people these days.

nodes.speaker: Phil
nodes.text: Er, right. So can we talk about that P.E. requirement? What exactly do I have to do?

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Well, Spike, the school requires that you get a certain number of hours a week.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: But our records indicate you've been skipping.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I may have skipped once or twice... Or ten times...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: But it was in the spirit of P.E.! I went skating. Doesn't that count as physical activity?

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Unfortunately, we don't reward students that go rogue, so you still have to make up all your hours.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: As that's impossible to do in two days, I'm afraid the only other option is summer school.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Summer school? For P.E.?

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Oh wait, unless you were part of a sports team.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Sports team?

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Yes, the senior year P.E. requirement can be waived if you played a sport.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: You aren't on a team, are you?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Uh... What if I was?

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Well, if that's the case, you need to have your Coach sign off on this form.
Ms. Lee hands Spike a piece of paper.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Then you need to turn it in, so I can pass it by Principal Shapiro and process it.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: That's it? And I'll be done with P.E.?

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: That's what I said, isn't it?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Thanks, Ms. Lee!
Spike leaves the counselor's office.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: So all I have to do is prove that I'm part of a sports team.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: But how am I going to do that?

nodes.speaker: Kim
nodes.text: Spike! Hey!
Spike turns to see Kim holding a huge box of trophies. Spike rushes to help her carry them.

nodes.speaker: Kim
nodes.text: Thanks, Spike.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: What is all this?

nodes.speaker: Kim
nodes.text: Oh, there's a banquet for all the students involved in sports.

nodes.speaker: Kim
nodes.text: Since I'm the captain of the girls' basketball team, I'm helping them organize and set it up.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: That's cool. It sounds like you girls deserve a banquet or two.

nodes.speaker: Kim
nodes.text: The season went pretty smoothly for us. But we are losing some of our best girls this year... I mean, Mallika's graduating.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: That's hard.

nodes.speaker: Kim
nodes.text: Yeah well, it happens. Hey, what's new with you? I saw you coming out of Ms. Lee's office. Something wrong?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Kind of. I might not graduate... Unless I can get on a sports team to waive the P.E. requirement.

nodes.speaker: Kim
nodes.text: I knew skipping P.E. was going to come back to haunt you. But that's serious.

nodes.speaker: Kim
nodes.text: Hey, you need to join a sports team? Why don't you join the boys' basketball team?

nodes.speaker: Kim
nodes.text: They're playing their last game, and they could use a substitute. If you do that, then for sure their Coach will sign your papers.

nodes.speaker: Kim
nodes.text: They're a little desperate for a fifth player.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: That's a great idea! I'll check it out after school. Thanks, Kim!

nodes.speaker: Kim
nodes.text: No prob.
In the gym that afternoon...

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: Good work on that play, guys!

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: Don't you think it would work better if we actually had another player?

nodes.speaker: Phil
nodes.text: Yeah, if only Erik hadn't quit. Who knew you could even develop a phobia of dropping balls in baskets?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Jacob! Heard you needed a fifth.

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: Depends on who's applying.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I am!

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: I didn't know you played basketball.

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: You any good?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Well, you see, I haven't really played...

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: Then why do you want to join the basketball team again?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Jacob's one of those guys who takes his sport very seriously...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I heard he even used female team-building skills in order to win!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Uh, I'm joining because...

options.label: I want to try something new.

nodes.text: But not `quite` perfectly. Play again to move onto the perfect ending!
nodes.text_bbcode: But not [b]quite[/b] perfectly. Play again to move onto the perfect ending!

The next day, Spike hurries to the graduation ceremony...
And finds an angry Ms. Lee waiting right outside!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Nuh uh. No way. You are `not` going in there.
nodes.text_bbcode: Nuh uh. No way. You are [color=#3b78e2][i]not[/i][/color] going in there.

nodes.speaker: Chip
nodes.text: What? Why not?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: You can't go into the graduation ceremony, Mr. Chapman, because you are `not` graduating.
nodes.text_bbcode: You can't go into the graduation ceremony, Mr. Chapman, because you are [color=#3b78e2][i]not[/i][/color] graduating.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: But... I have to graduate!

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Oh really? Did you complete all of your requirements?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Well... No... Not technically...

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Then I can't even begin to understand why we're having this conversation!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Well... Can I at least go in to see my girlfriend? See, she's graduating, and it would mean a lot to her if I...

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Ahem. As deeply moved as I am by your desire to see your special lady...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I prefer the term 'girlfriend'...

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Whatever the term, I just don't think it would be good for the rest of the students to see you there.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: They're at the peaks of their lives... Dreaming of a brighter, better future.... Boundless opportunities in front of them...

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: And you, well... Let's just say you'll lower the tone.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Maybe I can be a potent cautionary tale?

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Oh, don't worry, sweetie. You'll be that no matter what!
Ms. Lee turns and walks off. Spike watches her go...
The next morning, Spike waits nervously in front of the school.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: An hour before graduation, and I still haven't heard from Ms. Lee!
Around him, students in robes and mortarboards file into the auditorium...

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: Whoo hoo! I'm going to graduate!

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: I don't know how you pulled that one off...

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: I told Mr. Chetty I'd beat him up if he didn't give me an 'A'!

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: So awesome...

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: Next year, Ryan. You can make it.
The two boys run inside.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Come on, Travis is graduating? I've got to be in the running...
In the lot, Spike can see Ms. Lee getting out of her car. He runs up to her.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Hello, Spike. I'm sure you're excited to hear the verdict.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Principal Shapiro looked at all your paperwork, and...

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: You're graduating!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Whoo! Yeah! `Yeah!`
nodes.text_bbcode: Whoo! Yeah! [color=#e23b3b][i]Yeah![/i][/color]

nodes.text: Spike dances around the lot.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: I was going to tell you yesterday when the news came in, but I thought it'd make for a better surprise.
They proudly walk into the auditorium...
During the graduation ceremony, Principal Shapiro takes the stage.

nodes.speaker: Shapiro
nodes.text: Thank you, Phineas Shovelplow Angus, for your wonderful valedictorian speech.

nodes.speaker: Shapiro
nodes.text: And now for the moment you've been waiting for... I'll be calling you up one by one to receive your high school diploma!
The students line up, each taking a diploma as they come forward.

nodes.speaker: Shapiro
nodes.text: Lydia Carter, please come forward for your diploma... Jackie Carnine, please come forward for your diploma...

nodes.speaker: Shapiro
nodes.text: Spike Chapman, please come forward and collect your diploma...
Spike walks up to the stage to receive his diploma!
From the crowd, there's a cheer from Spike's friends and family!

nodes.speaker: Denni
nodes.text: Goooooo, Spike!

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: Congrats, man!

nodes.speaker: Kenji
nodes.text: Knew you had it in you.

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Chapman
nodes.text: That's my son! Good job, Spike!

nodes.speaker: Chip
nodes.text: Yay, big bro! ...But is the ceremony over yet?
Principal Shapiro shakes Spike's hand.

nodes.speaker: Shapiro
nodes.text: Good work getting all your requirements done, Spike.

nodes.speaker: Shapiro
nodes.text: I believe you have a bright future ahead of you.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Thanks, Principal Shapiro!
Spike walks excitedly off stage as Principal Shapiro continues to call names.

nodes.speaker: Shapiro
nodes.text: Joe Cleveton... Angela Danworth... Mallika Desai...

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Yay! I'm done!
One by one, the names of Spike's classmates get called until finally...

nodes.speaker: Shapiro
nodes.text: And that is the last name. I now present to you...

nodes.speaker: Shapiro
nodes.text: The class of 2011! Congratulations to everyone!
Mortarboards are thrown up with loud shouts and hoots!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Woo hoo!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Yeah!
Spike and Mallika hug as graduation hats fall around them.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: `Yeah.`
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#e23b3b][i]Yeah.[/i][/color]

nodes.text: At the graduation afterparty...
The graduates and their friends eat ice cream and pizza!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: I feel like I'm in grade school again with all this food.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I'm not complaining!
As Spike settles into eating...

nodes.speaker: Scott
nodes.text: So, Spike, you figured out `how` you were going to graduate...
nodes.text_bbcode: So, Spike, you figured out [color=#e23b3b][i]how[/i][/color] you were going to graduate...

nodes.speaker: Scott
nodes.text: But what are you going to do now?

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Oh, Spike doesn't have to answer that.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: No, it's okay. I don't know what I'm going to do honestly.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I'm sure I'll figure it out. It feels like the future's wide open.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: But the first thing I'm going to do is finish this pizza!
And meanwhile on the other side of the restaurant...
Travis and Ryan kick an old-fashioned jukebox for quarters.

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: So how do ya feel now that you're all old and graduated?

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: The same. No difference. It's dumb.

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: You're telling me. What are you going to do now?

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: Community college.

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: That's tough.

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: Well, my dad promised me an awesome job at his auto shop if I got a degree.

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: So I'm gonna spend half my time at Centerscore Community.

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: What are you going to do with the other half?

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: Hang out with you.

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: Really? You're finally free of this dump, and you're going to come back to it?

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: Well, who else am I going to hang out with?

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: Good point. You are smart, you lugnut.
And elsewhere...

nodes.speaker: Howard
nodes.text: It feels weird to know that all the people that have graduated won't be around next year.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: I agree. I've gotten so used to how things are. I wonder how different it'll be next year.

nodes.speaker: Howard
nodes.text: There'll be new faces, different cliques...

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: At least we have each other.

nodes.speaker: Howard
nodes.text: Always.
Later that evening, $ZOE returns home to find Aunt Cathy sorting through the mail at the table.

nodes.speaker: Aunt Cathy
nodes.text: $ZOE! Good timing! Just the girl I wanted to see.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Hi, Aunt Cathy! What's up?

nodes.speaker: Aunt Cathy
nodes.text: You just got this letter in the mail today.
Aunt Cathy hands $ZOE a letter.
As $ZOE reads it, her fingers tighten on the paper and her face goes pale.

nodes.speaker: Aunt Cathy
nodes.text: You okay? You look as white as a ghost!

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Sorry, Aunt Cathy. It's... Nothing.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: I...I have to go.
$ZOE flees from the room.
Uh-oh! Just what's in that letter that $ZOE received?
Looks like someone's in trouble... But, at least, it's not Spike!
His graduation went off without a hitch! All thanks to you! You played a great game!

args.text: Thanks for playing! See you in another episode!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: It's okay... It's no big deal.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: So I didn't graduate this year! That's fine! I'll graduate `next year!` I'll turn it all around!
nodes.text_bbcode: So I didn't graduate this year! That's fine! I'll graduate [color=#e23b3b][i]next year![/i][/color] I'll turn it all around!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: 2012 is the year of Spike!
One year later, in Ms. Lee's office...

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Nope! No can do, Spike! You `still` haven't completed your graduation requirements!
nodes.text_bbcode: Nope! No can do, Spike! You [color=#3b78e2][i]still[/i][/color] haven't completed your graduation requirements!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I got distracted!

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Well, you're just going to have to come back next year!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Okay, okay... It's fine... No big deal...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: 2013... The year I graduate!
One year later...

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: I don't know how this is possible, but you somehow completed even fewer requirements than last year! You actually `lost` academic credits!
nodes.text_bbcode: I don't know how this is possible, but you somehow completed even fewer requirements than last year! You actually [color=#3b78e2][i]lost[/i][/color] academic credits!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I'm easily distracted!

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Yeah, well, you're stuck here... Again!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: That's fine... That's fine... 2014... Everything's coming up Spike!
And one year after that...

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Are you not getting tired of this? Because I am getting absolutely exhausted of telling you that you can't graduate!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Things aren't fine, are they?

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: No, Mr. Chapman. No they aren't.
Twenty-three years later...
Spike walks down the hall of Centerscore High on the last day of school...

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Mr. Chapman! Looking as young and hearty as ever!

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: If only you were as good at taking tests as you are at being handsome, you might be graduating!
Ms. Lee walks off... And a sharply-dressed young man pops around the corner!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Man, was Ms. Lee just hitting on me?

nodes.speaker: Hector Jr.
nodes.text: Sure sounds like that, buddy! Zwinks!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Zwinks? I... I don't know what that means...

nodes.speaker: Hector Jr.
nodes.text: It's the new slang! Jeez! You are `so` bubonic! Taddles!
nodes.text_bbcode: It's the new slang! Jeez! You are [color=#e23b3b][i]so[/i][/color] bubonic! Taddles!

nodes.text: Hector Jr. glides off on his hoverboard. Spike sadly watches him go...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Say hi to your dad for me!

nodes.speaker: Hector Jr.
nodes.text: Whateverest!
Hector Jr. vanishes around a corner...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Aw man. I miss the old gang... Howard... Colt... Regular Hector...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Not to mention Mallika. I heard she just got married. I hope he's treating her well... Being the Vice President, he's probably busy a lot...
Just as Spike is about to totally lose himself in his memories... A meaty hand lands on his shoulder!

nodes.speaker: Travis Two
nodes.text: Yo! Gramps!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Oh, hey Travis Two. Man, you are even `bigger` than your dad...
nodes.text_bbcode: Oh, hey Travis Two. Man, you are even [color=#e23b3b][i]bigger[/i][/color] than your dad...

nodes.speaker: Travis Two
nodes.text: I drink my milk. Now gimme your lunch money!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Look, dude, I... I need to pay the rent this week... Can't I just, I don't know, get you an IOU?

nodes.speaker: Travis Two
nodes.text: Less talking, more pay up! Unless you want a taste of my cyber-knuckles...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Okay, okay... Here...
Spike hands Travis Two a wad of cash. He pockets it and grins.

nodes.speaker: Travis Two
nodes.text: Zwinks!
Spike is the world's first 44-year senior... And he's getting bullied? That's a `terrible` ending!
nodes.text_bbcode: Spike is the world's first 44-year senior... And he's getting bullied? That's a [b]terrible[/b] ending!

nodes.text: Try again! You've got to be able to get a better ending than that!

args.text: Try again! We know you can do it!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I... I can't believe it! This is terrible!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: All my friends are going to leave... Mallika's going to be gone... And my mom's going to kick me out of my house!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: No... No! I am `not` letting his happen! I'm graduating this year, even if I have to break in there and graduate myself!
nodes.text_bbcode: No... No! I am [color=#e23b3b][i]not[/i][/color] letting his happen! I'm graduating this year, even if I have to break in there and graduate myself!

nodes.text: Spike turns to walk in... And sees Officer Monte standing outside, looking vigilantly!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Looks like they hired him to work security... Guess I'm not going in the front door...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Not like that's guy's every stopped me!
A few minutes later, in the Centerscore auditorium... Principal Shapiro is reading the list of graduating students!

nodes.speaker: Shapiro
nodes.text: Joe Cleveton... Angela Danworth... Mallika Desai...
Mallika steps onto the stage to take her diploma... When there's suddenly a lurching, creaky noise from the air vent!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: That doesn't sound good...
The vent gives way... And Spike tumbles out, slamming onto the ground!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Oooooof!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: `Spike?!`
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#3b78e2][i]Spike?![/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Shapiro
nodes.text: What... What is this?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I... I was hoping to come out at the back of the room...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I just... Wanted to graduate...

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Spike, I know you don't think that's how it works...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Well, what else am I supposed to, Mallika? What else am I supposed to...
Just then, the door swings open! Officer Monte rushes in!

nodes.speaker: Officer Monte
nodes.text: Freeze right there, rabble-rouser!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Wait, sir, I... I'm not rousing any rabble! I swear!

nodes.speaker: Officer Monte
nodes.text: That's `exactly` what a rabble-rouser would say!
nodes.text_bbcode: That's [color=#e23b3b][i]exactly[/i][/color] what a rabble-rouser would say!

nodes.text: Officer Monte whips out a taser and fires, nailing Spike in the chest!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Spike!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: `Aghghghghghghghgh!`
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#e23b3b][i]Aghghghghghghghgh![/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Officer Monte
nodes.text: Got him!
Spike lays on the ground, whimpering sadly...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I just... Wanted... To graduate...
Ouch! Spike's day was embarrassing and pathetic... Not to mention painful!
Try again! We know you can get a better ending than that!

args.text: Try again! We know you can do it!

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: So if that's all...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Actually, there's one last thing. I also need to get my community service hours, right?

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: According to our files... There are no records of your working for your community.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: So what should I do?

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: If you had come earlier in the year, we'd try to figure out your interests...

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Your potential career, the college you'd like to go to, and we'd try to personalize your service experience.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Unluckily, however, we'll just have to find whatever opportunity comes up next.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Okay... So where do I start?

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: I have no idea! Why don't you go ask around and see what you come up with?

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Then have someone write a report to me about it! Good luck!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I... But...

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Bye bye now.
Spike leaves.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Well, I certainly won't miss that when I'm gone...
Spike walks down the hall.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: If I were a community service organizer, where would I be?
Down the hall, Spike sees Denni struggling to carry a bunch of food items!
Spike rushes over to help!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Easy there... You're carrying a lot of stuff!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Whoa, is that an entire turkey?!

nodes.speaker: Denni
nodes.text: Yeah, and here I thought my days of carting food back and forth were over.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Well, if you need someone to take it off your hands...

nodes.speaker: Denni
nodes.text: Unfortunately, this food is going to a charity fundraiser dinner I'm holding.

nodes.speaker: Denni
nodes.text: But you can help me carry it.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Sure thing.
They trek the food across campus to the gym where a fancy-looking dinner is being set up.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I like what you've done with the place.

nodes.speaker: Denni
nodes.text: Yeah, it barely looks like the cafeteria at all, right?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: You're organizing a fundraiser on your own?

nodes.speaker: Denni
nodes.text: Not exactly. I'm working with W.H.A.L.E. My group's been picking up a lot of community service hours lately to fund our summer trip to build houses.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Community service hours? Hey, does your group need another hand by any chance?

nodes.speaker: Denni
nodes.text: Yes! Between the banquet and the upcoming Fourth of July celebration, we're swamped.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: It just so happens I need community service hours in order to graduate...

nodes.speaker: Denni
nodes.text: Well, we do need some people to help at the skate park...

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Perfect!

nodes.speaker: Denni
nodes.text: Okay! Then see you later, around four?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Yes!
Later that day, at four...
Spike meets up with Denni at the skate park.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: All right, what are we going to do? Build new ramps, do some tricks? Skate?
Denni hands Spike some rags and a bottle of solvent.

nodes.speaker: Denni
nodes.text: It looks a lot like cleaning up the graffiti on the walls.
Denni shows Spike how to clean it.

nodes.speaker: Denni
nodes.text: Then after you wait some time, you can scrub it away. See?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I can't believe some people. 'Travus waz hear'... 'Books suck!'... 'Space 'Splosions Rules'?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Why would anyone be tempted to write on the wall?

nodes.speaker: Denni
nodes.text: Ahem.
Denni points to another set of words on the wall farther down.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: 'Spike is number one'... Oh. I see.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Ha, I remember writing that now. This skate park is where I learned to skate. I thought it was all mine, so I needed to put my name up.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: This is weird.

nodes.speaker: Denni
nodes.text: Will you be okay?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Yeah, totally. I don't need my name on something to feel important.

nodes.speaker: Denni
nodes.text: Well, have fun. I have to go to the other side of the park to organize more workers. If you need me, you can give me a call.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: No problem.
Spike starts to clean, scrubbing away at the graffiti.
A couple hours later, Spike has made progress on the wall when he hears the sound of paint from a spray can!
Spike looks down the wall to see Ryan and Travis tagging it!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Hey, I just scrubbed over this entire wall!

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: So what?

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: Scrub off, twerp. We're marking this as our territory now.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I'm not a twerp. Where's Spencer, your new ringleader?

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: He doesn't control us.

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: Yeah, not when we're off campus!

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: Not at `all,` you moron. Now are you going to get out of our way or what?
nodes.text_bbcode: Not at [color=#e23b3b][i]all,[/i][/color] you moron. Now are you going to get out of our way or what?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Come on, you guys don't want to do this.

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: Oh yeah? Why not?

options.label: There are better things to do.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I understand, Ms. Lee.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Well, Spike, except for your final, you've done everything you can for yourself.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: We'll see what the principal says once she reviews your file.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: I'm sure this is a very exciting time in your life.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: What Principal Shapiro says will be the difference between graduating and moving forward with your life...

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Or being stuck here, trapped forever in a downward spiral of your own underachievement.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: But try not to stress out too much, Spike.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Yeah...

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: And be sure to ace your final... Or else you may never graduate.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Bye now!
Spike leaves.
It's the last day of class before graduation...
And Mallika is walking with Spike to his English class after lunch.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Good luck on your final.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: No pressure or anything. I just have to get a 'C' or else flunk out of high school... Again.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: When I say it like that, it sounds hopeless.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: But you studied!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: You'll do great, I know it.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: I'll meet you after school in the parking lot?

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Yeah.
Spike kisses Mallika.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Bye.
During the final...

nodes.speaker: Ms. Prez
nodes.text: You have an hour to finish the test. No talking. When you're done, turn your test over and sit quietly until everyone else is finished.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Prez
nodes.text: All right then. You can begin.
Spike looks down at the first question on his test.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: I came to watch your basketball game to see if your Coach would sign off on the papers.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: Surprisingly, he gave a glowing report of your performance and said he'd wished you joined the team earlier.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: I'm sure Principal Shapiro's going to have no issue waiving your P.E. credit.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Great!

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: I received a very satisfactory report from your superior. This might be hard to believe, but...

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: She said you did a wonderful job cleaning up the old park, and she believes more people will be willing to spend their time there.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Lee
nodes.text: At any rate, this will look good when I run this report past the principal.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: The nerds did help me a lot.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I just need to remember what they told me.
In fact, you were `perfect!` Here's your bonus scene!
nodes.text_bbcode: In fact, you were [b]perfect![/b] Here's your bonus scene!

nodes.text: Let's check in and see what some of our favorite Centerscore students are doing this summer!
In the park, Mallika films while Spike acts as an alien for the nerds in their new movie.

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: I got a good angle on this tree over here, guys. So whenever you're ready...
Mallika goes quiet.
Erik walks into the camera frame and stops in the middle, his hand to his forehead in a salute.

nodes.speaker: Erik
nodes.text: Captain Dextrous, I have secured an alien from this planet!

nodes.speaker: Erik
nodes.text: He does not seem to be overly hostile.

nodes.speaker: Erik
nodes.text: In fact, he seems rather friendly.

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: Good work, Lieutenant, uh, Ericson. Let us question the alien.

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: Alien, what kind of creature are you?
Erik nudges Spike.

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Oh, uh, what was my line again? Oh, right!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: I am a Grenhair alien. From the planet Grenhaira. All hail Captain Quarch!
The scene goes on.

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: And that is why we must go forth and find the Sacred Crystal of Enlightenment!

nodes.speaker: Erik
nodes.text: Go forth!

nodes.speaker: Spike
nodes.text: Go forth!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: And cut! Okay, from the top!

nodes.speaker: Mallika
nodes.text: Captain Dextrous, I need more emotion from you. Erik, I need more depth from you. And Spike... Keep up the green hair.
In the park one fine afternoon in late June...
$Scott holds Angie's hand as they walk along a lane in the park.

nodes.speaker: Scott
nodes.text: Isn't this the life?

nodes.speaker: Angie
nodes.text: Sunshine, a cool breeze, the green grass...

nodes.speaker: Scott
nodes.text: Yeah. I could just stay out here all day, napping under that tree.

nodes.speaker: Justin
nodes.text: Not so fast, Vice President.

nodes.speaker: Scott
nodes.text: Hello, Justin.
Justin approaches the couple.

nodes.speaker: Justin
nodes.text: You two ready to work?

nodes.speaker: Angie
nodes.text: Of course. That's why we're here. $Scott and I would never slack.

nodes.speaker: Scott
nodes.text: Nope. Never.

nodes.speaker: Justin
nodes.text: We only have a couple weeks to organize and set up the fairgrounds for the Fourth of July celebration.

nodes.speaker: Justin
nodes.text: Now I was thinking the fair booths will run along the lake...

nodes.speaker: Angie
nodes.text: The booths should probably be closer to the shade, shouldn't they?

nodes.speaker: Justin
nodes.text: But they'll be more popular if they're in an open area...

nodes.speaker: Angie
nodes.text: Not if people want to spend more time in the shade on a hot afternoon.

nodes.speaker: Justin
nodes.text: All right, what if we put them to one side of the lake, but near the grove of trees?

nodes.speaker: Angie
nodes.text: Deal.

nodes.speaker: Justin
nodes.text: Deal.

nodes.speaker: Scott
nodes.text: And to think, other couples would just spend their summers together making out.

nodes.speaker: Scott
nodes.text: We get to spend it making a festival... With Justin.
And while some students have events to plan or just plain fun to have...
Sam is at home, trying to comfort $ZOE.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Come on, $ZOE. You know you can tell me anything.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Not this time, Sam.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: We're friends, aren't we? You can trust me, right?

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: It's not that. It's just... I can't talk about it.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Is there anything I can do to help?

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: No, there's nothing you can do. I'm sorry. I really am.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: But I think I need to be alone now.
Sam nods and leaves the room.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: What am I going to do?
$ZOE flops onto her bed and starts sobbing into her pillow.
